style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: Three verses on unity, and two of the strangest similes in Scripture. David looks at brothers dwelling together as one -- pilgrims crowded into Jerusalem for the feast, tribes that spent the rest of the year apart -- and says: behold, how good and how pleasant. Then he reaches for pictures that only make sense from inside the covenant. Unity is like the anointing oil poured on Aaron's head, so lavish it runs down his beard and onto the collar of his priestly robes -- consecration overflowing from the head to the whole body, the picture Paul would later make of Christ and His church. And it is like the dew of Hermon, the great northern mountain whose heavy night-moisture keeps its slopes green through the dry season, that dew somehow falling on the dry hills of Zion -- refreshment from the far north arriving in the south, life carried where it could not have grown. Both images move downward: oil from the head, dew from the mountain. Unity is not something brothers manufacture upward; it is a blessing that descends. And the last line says exactly that: there, in that togetherness, the LORD has commanded the blessing -- life forevermore.

1.text: A song of ascents, of David. Look -- how good and how pleasant it is when brothers dwell together as one!
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth] of David. Behold, how good [tov] and how pleasant [naim -- delightful, sweet] it is for brethren [ach] to dwell [yashab] together ['even together', gam yachad, the KJV margin] in unity!
1.notes: hinneh -- look at it: unity is pointed at like a sight worth stopping for. tov and naim (H2896, H5273), good AND pleasant -- right and also lovely, the pair of Psalm 135:3. achim yashab gam yachad (H251, H3427, H3162): brothers not merely near but sitting down together, the yachad of Jerusalem's compact walls (cf. Psalm 122:3).

2.text: It is like the fine oil poured on the head, running down onto the beard -- Aaron's beard -- running down to the collar of his robes;
2.amp: It is like the precious [tov] ointment [shemen -- the anointing oil] upon the head [rosh], that ran down [yarad] upon the beard [zaqan], even Aaron's [Aharon] beard: that went down [yarad] to the skirts ['mouth', peh -- the collar-opening] of his garments [middah].
2.notes: The shemen ha-tov (H8081) is the holy anointing oil of Exodus 30, poured on Aharon (H175) at his consecration -- and yarad (H3381) twice: it does not dab, it RUNS, head to zaqan to the peh middah (H6310, H4060), the collar of the ephod where the twelve tribes' names sat. Unity as consecration flowing from the Head down over the whole body (cf. Ephesians 4:15-16; 1 Corinthians 12:12).

3.text: It is like the dew of Hermon coming down upon the mountains of Zion -- for there the LORD has commanded the blessing: life forevermore.
3.amp: As the dew [tal] of Hermon [Chermon], and as the dew that descended [yarad] upon the mountains [har] of Zion [Tsiyyon]: for there the LORD [YHWH] commanded [tsavah] the blessing [berakah], even life [chay] for evermore [olam].
3.notes: The tal (H2919) of Chermon (H2768), the snow-capped giant of the north, is so heavy it soaks tents by dawn; Tsiyyon's hills are dry limestone. The picture is a miracle of transport -- northern refreshment yarad (H3381) onto southern rock, life arriving where it could not originate. And 'there' -- sham, in the place of brothers dwelling as one -- YHWH tsavah (H6680) the berakah, commanded it like a standing order: chayyim ad-olam. Unity is where God has decided to station eternal life (cf. John 17:21-23).
